newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end shade lower, hit by probe report.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end shade lower, hit by probe report.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly lower on Thursday after selling sparked by a newspaper report wiped out early gains, brokers said.
The index ended 0.12 points lower at 678.74, after rising to a day high of 689.12.

The Kookmin Ilbo newspaper said state prosecutors probed suspicion of price manipulation of shares in Dae Young Packaging Co, Daesung Electric Wire Co and Jungil Industrial Co. The prosectuion denied the report.
The report also hit other shares which had risen sharply in recent months, brokers said.
Shares of the three companies fell to their daily limits. Dae Young fell 4,300 won to 50,100, Daesung Electric 5,800 won to 67,200 and Jungil 5,300 won to 61,700.
"The report quickly chilled sentiment," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
"Investors were unsure whether this would lead to a big drop or fizzle out soon. But they just wanted to stay away at the moment," Koh said.
Kookmin Ilbo said there was suspicion that manipulation was responsible for an increase of up to 350 percent in the share prices of the three companies in a short period last year.

Finance minister Kang Kyong-shik's remarks that the economy was in serious trouble had no major impact. Kang told reporters that drastic measures were needed to resolve the deep-rooted economic problem of "high-cost and low efficiency".
Blue chips rose across the board in the morning but many lost ground to close flat or lower.
Korea Electric Power ended unchanged at 26,500 won, while SK Telecom fell 19,000 won to 466,000.
June futures closed 0.50 points higher at 67.45 and the KOSPI-200 index ended 0.23 points higher at 69.12.
